scoring_justification: Only the final aggregated JSON is submitted; full recompute from raw spectral curves is infeasible. We compare the agent's reported per-beam and total efficiencies to the paper's hidden gold with absolute tolerance ±0.5% and verify internal consistency by recomputing total η from per-beam values.

hidden_assets.purpose: Gold per-beam and total efficiencies for two-channel (w=0.1, 0.3 nm) and three-channel (w=0.1, 0.3 nm) SBC combining from the paper's Tables 1 and 2.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted directly from the paper's tables.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the paper's reported results, traceable to specific rows and columns.

required.two_channel: array of objects with fields w (number, nm), eta_T (number, %), eta_D (number, %), eta (number, %)
required.three_channel: array of objects with fields w (number, nm), eta_1D (number, %), eta_2T_prime (number, %), eta_1T (number, %), eta_1T_prime (number, %), eta_2D (number, %), eta (number, %)

outputs.description: Two‑channel and three‑channel SBC combining efficiencies and their intermediate per‑beam diffraction/transmission efficiencies for spectral widths 0.1 nm and 0.3 nm. The hidden checker compares the reported values against paper‑derived gold thresholds (threshold_or_better).

output_contract.notes: The agent must implement the diffraction efficiency model from Kogelnik’s coupled‑wave theory using the given grating parameters. No external dataset is required.
